discovered.citation: Du, M., Khazatsky, A., Gerstenberg, T., & Finn, C. (2024). To Err is Robotic: Rapid Value-Based Trial-and-Error during Deployment. arXiv:2406.15917. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15917
discovered.relevance: The most direct match for retry-with-adjusted-strategy: Bellman-Guided Retrials monitors a base policy's progress with a learned value function, detects when the current attempt is failing, aborts before an unrecoverable mistake, recovers, and resamples a new strategy explicitly skewed away from behaviors that recently failed in the episode. Improves base-policy success rates by over 20% in simulation and 50% on real-robot experiments, demonstrating episodic self-correction during deployment without retraining.

discovered.citation: Liu, Z., Bahety, A., & Song, S. (2023). REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction. Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2023. arXiv:2306.15724. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15724
discovered.relevance: Canonical episodic self-correction work: converts the robot's own multisensory execution history into a hierarchical experience summary, queries an LLM to progressively diagnose why the attempt failed, and feeds the failure explanation to a language-based planner that generates a correction plan for the retry. Introduces the RoboFail benchmark of failure scenarios and validates correction planning in simulation and on a real robot arm.

discovered.citation: Huang, W., Xia, F., Xiao, T., Chan, H., Liang, J., Florence, P., Zeng, A., Tompson, J., Mordatch, I., Chebotar, Y., Sermanet, P., Brown, N., Jackson, T., Luu, L., Levine, S., Hausman, K., & Ichter, B. (2022). Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models. Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2022. arXiv:2207.05608. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05608
discovered.relevance: Foundational 2022 demonstration of in-context adaptation on real robots: closes the planning loop by injecting success detection, scene descriptions, and other environment feedback into the LLM prompt, so when a skill fails the planner observes the failure and retries or replans in-context, without any additional training. Validated on real tabletop rearrangement and kitchen mobile-manipulation robots, establishing the feedback-driven retry paradigm that later self-correction work builds on.

discovered.citation: Dai, Y., Lee, J., Fazeli, N., & Chai, J. (2024). RACER: Rich Language-Guided Failure Recovery Policies for Imitation Learning. ICRA 2025. arXiv:2409.14674. https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14674
discovered.relevance: Trains failure recovery directly into the policy: a scalable pipeline augments expert demonstrations with failure-and-recovery trajectories annotated with fine-grained language, and a VLM supervisor provides online corrective language guidance to a language-conditioned visuomotor actor when execution goes wrong. Outperforms RVT on RLBench long-horizon, goal-change, and zero-shot tasks and transfers to real-world robot evaluation, showing learned (rather than scripted) retry/recovery behavior.

discovered.citation: Bousmalis, K., Vezzani, G., Rao, D., et al. (Google DeepMind) (2023). RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation. Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR). arXiv:2306.11706. https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11706
discovered.relevance: Demonstrates the self-improvement loop at scale on real robot arms: a multi-embodiment goal-conditioned decision transformer practices new tasks autonomously, and its self-generated trajectories (its own attempts, successful and otherwise) are folded back into training for the next iteration, improving performance across tasks with only 100-1000 human examples per new task. Relevant as the strongest evidence that robots can improve from their own attempt data across episodes, complementing within-episode retry methods.

discovered.citation: Guo, Y., Wang, Y.-J., Zha, L., Jiang, Z., & Chen, J. (2023). DoReMi: Grounding Language Model by Detecting and Recovering from Plan-Execution Misalignment. IROS/ICRA (IEEE) 2024. arXiv:2307.00329. https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00329
discovered.relevance: Addresses aborted/deviating attempts at the plan-execution interface: the LLM generates both the plan and executability constraints, a VLM continuously checks those constraints during low-level execution, and any detected violation immediately triggers LLM re-planning to recover and re-attempt the step. Evaluated on robot-arm manipulation and humanoid tasks with higher success rates and shorter execution times, exemplifying immediate detection-and-recovery rather than open-loop replay.

discovered.citation: B. Thananjeyan, A. Balakrishna, S. Nair, M. Luo, K. Srinivasan, M. Hwang, J. E. Gonzalez, J. Ibarz, C. Finn, and K. Goldberg, "Recovery RL: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Learned Recovery Zones," IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, vol. 6, no. 3, pp. 4915-4922, 2021. arXiv:2010.15920. https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15920
discovered.relevance: The canonical safe-RL recovery-policy paper: it splits control between a task policy and a dedicated recovery policy that takes over when a learned constraint-violation critic (trained on offline data) predicts the agent is entering an unsafe zone. This is the archetype of an 'active abort' mechanism in safe RL — a learned monitor triggering a learned safe-termination/recovery behavior — validated in simulation and on a physical robot obstacle-avoidance task.

discovered.citation: K.-C. Hsu, A. Z. Ren, D. P. Nguyen, A. Majumdar, and J. F. Fisac, "Sim-to-Lab-to-Real: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Shielding and Generalization Guarantees," Artificial Intelligence, vol. 314, 103811, 2023. arXiv:2201.08355. https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08355
discovered.relevance: Dual-policy safe RL in which a backup (safety) policy is trained via the Safety Bellman Equation from Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and a supervisory shield decides at runtime when to abort the performance policy and hand control to the backup. Adds PAC-Bayes generalization bounds on safety for deployment in unseen environments — directly relevant as a principled learned-safety-monitor-plus-recovery-controller architecture transferable to aerial navigation.

discovered.citation: A. Banerjee, K. Rahmani, J. Biswas, and I. Dillig, "Dynamic Model Predictive Shielding for Provably Safe Reinforcement Learning," Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024). arXiv:2405.13863. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13863
discovered.relevance: Extends model predictive shielding: instead of a fixed static backup policy, a local planner dynamically synthesizes safe recovery actions that preserve provable safety while still maximizing short- and long-term reward, so aborts recover toward task progress rather than mere stopping. Useful as the state of the art on making abort/recovery interventions less conservative in provably safe RL.

discovered.citation: L. Bartolomei, Y. Kompis, L. Teixeira, and M. Chli, "Autonomous Emergency Landing for Multicopters using Deep Reinforcement Learning," Proc. IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), Kyoto, 2022, pp. 3392-3399. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9981152/
discovered.relevance: Directly on active abort in aerial robotics: a deep-RL pipeline (ETH Zurich Vision for Robotics Lab) for aborting a multicopter mission under emergencies such as mechanical malfunction, low battery, localization failure, or GPS jamming, using semantic and depth input to steer toward safe landing areas as fast as possible under safety constraints. Code released (VIS4ROB-lab/multirotors_landing), making it a strong practical baseline for learned emergency-termination behaviors on drones.

discovered.citation: I. R. Ward, M. Paral, K. Riordan, and M. J. Kochenderfer, "Improving the Resilience of Quadrotors in Underground Environments by Combining Learning-based and Safety Controllers," Proc. 11th International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies (CoDIT), 2025. arXiv:2509.02808. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02808
discovered.relevance: A concrete learned safety monitor for drones: a normalizing-flow prior over environment observations serves as a runtime out-of-distribution detector that triggers a switch from the fast learned navigation controller to a conservative safety controller with collision-avoidance guarantees. Directly relevant as evidence for monitor-triggered fallback (abort-to-safe-controller) architectures on quadrotors in degraded environments.

discovered.citation: A. Zhao, Y. Zhong, K. Hoi, J. Mou, J. Wang, L. Wang, J. Hou, and F. Gao, "Agile Fall Recovery for Quadrotors with Bidirectional Thrust via Reinforcement Learning," arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.16513, 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16513
discovered.relevance: Recent (June 2026) recovery-controller work: an RL policy (recurrent, asymmetric actor-critic with an INDI inner loop) that recovers a quadrotor from arbitrary post-failure ground attitudes to stable hover using only lightweight onboard sensors, with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer under wind and payload disturbances. Covers the post-abort/post-crash recovery end of the pipeline — what a learned policy can do after a termination or fall event rather than just avoiding one.

discovered.citation: J. Lin, L. Wang, F. Gao, S. Shen, and F. Zhang, "Flying through a narrow gap using neural network: an end-to-end planning and control approach," IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2019. arXiv:1903.09088. https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.09088
discovered.relevance: Foundational imitate-then-reinforce framework: an end-to-end policy network imitates a traditional planner/controller and is fine-tuned with RL to fly a quadrotor through tilted narrow gaps (state-based input, not raw vision).

discovered.citation: C. Xiao, P. Lu, and Q. He, "Flying Through a Narrow Gap Using End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning Augmented With Curriculum Learning and Sim2Real," IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, vol. 34, no. 5, pp. 2701-2708, 2023. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9530254/
discovered.relevance: End-to-end deep RL with curriculum learning to overcome the sparse reward behind the gap, plus a Sim2Real transfer scheme demonstrated on a real quadrotor without real-flight training data.

discovered.citation: Y. Xie, M. Lu, R. Peng, and P. Lu, "Learning Agile Flights Through Narrow Gaps with Varying Angles Using Onboard Sensing," IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, vol. 8, 2023. arXiv:2302.11233. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11233
discovered.relevance: Deep RL policy that traverses unknown, tilted narrow gaps using gap detection from a single onboard camera, handling varying gap angles with aggressive attitude alignment.

discovered.citation: J. Xing, A. Romero, L. Bauersfeld, and D. Scaramuzza, "Bootstrapping Reinforcement Learning with Imitation for Vision-Based Agile Flight," Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL), Munich, 2024. arXiv:2403.12203. https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12203
discovered.relevance: Combines RL performance with imitation-learning sample efficiency to train visuomotor policies (raw pixels to commands) for agile flight through racing gates/window-like openings.

discovered.citation: T. Wu, G. Xu, Z. Wang, J. Lin, T. Chen, Y. Wu, Z. Han, Z. Liu, and F. Gao, "Precise aggressive aerial maneuvers with sensorimotor policies," Science Robotics, 2026. DOI: 10.1126/scirobotics.aeb0180. arXiv:2604.05828. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/scirobotics.aeb0180
discovered.relevance: RL-trained, distilled sensorimotor policy mapping onboard vision and proprioception directly to low-level commands, traversing gaps at 5 cm clearance and up to 90-degree tilt without prior gap pose knowledge.

discovered.citation: L. Zhang, Y. Hu, F. Yu, Y. Deng, W. Yu, and D. Zou, "Vision-Based End-to-End Learning for UAV Traversal of Irregular Gaps via Differentiable Simulation," arXiv:2604.02779, 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02779
discovered.relevance: End-to-end vision policy mapping depth images directly to control commands for agile traversal of narrow and irregular gaps, trained efficiently via differentiable simulation.
